correctness.rationale: For p in (0,h), the per-capita colonization term c(h-p)/[phi(1-h)+h+(gamma-1)p] has derivative -c[phi(1-h)+gamma h]/W(p)^2<0, giving a unique positive root precisely under ch>e[h+phi(1-h)]. Rearranged equilibrium balance U=(h-p)/e = (phi/c) + ((1-phi)/c)h + ((gamma-1)/c)p makes the design matrix rows (1,h,p), with a one-to-one map back to strictly positive c,phi,gamma. Full rank implies uniqueness; a nonzero kernel perturbation remains in the open positive parameter domain and maintains observed viable equilibria. The determinant of the three-survey L protocol is (h2-h1)(p3-p1) and strict negative dp*/de excludes zero. Exact rational inversion and counterexample checked; finite grids are corroboration only.

value.rationale: A minimal experimental-design theorem for recovering all three physically meaningful coefficients from exact positive equilibria fills an identifiable model-specific gap. It proves universal feasibility of an economical design and a sharp impossibility for surveys varying only one environmental control; these distinctions matter to mechanistic occupancy inference before statistical noise is considered.
